!faq

When will you be selling virtual land?

We are uncertain the dates of our public land sales at this time.  If you are reading this you have caught us at a very early stage, so congrats.  Hang in there with us, the first public land sale will be broadcast loud and clear on our socials.

What can you do with virtual land?

We are creating entire economies based upon the zones that the land is in.  For example, in “Life on the Farm”, you will be able to lease your land to farmers or farm it yourself, earning resources by trading your commodities. You can find more info in our whitepaper.

What will be the total land units for sale?

We will start with 600 plots per zone. (see whitepaper tokenomics for more info)

Will you have your own token?

Yes and first availability will be through a launchpad.  We have currently not yet decided which launchpad we will go with but we are determining the timeline to launch date now.

What can you do with the token?

Our primary token you will be able to buy land with.

When will you be selling NFTs?

We are hoping to be selling NFT’s by November.

What are your official channels?

Twitter:  @cornucopiasgame 
Discord: https://discord.gg/ZaavBkcGzJ
YouTube:  https://www.youtube.com/c/CornucopiasGame

Hey yall, might sound silly but could someone explain what launchpad is and why it has to be used to buy tokens?

Okay so this is kind of how I think about launchpads. 

Launchpads are like the venture capital companies of blockchain projects. So for example people come together and make this amazing project but need funding and so they go to a launchpad to help them get that funding to make that project a reality. So the launchpad will vet and if they’re going to take it on, market the project and help raise the capital (through an IDO/IGO/IMO) to get the project rolling. 

So to answer your question, in order to get involved in the initial sale of the project’s tokens, one usually needs to buy and stake the launchpad’s tokens first (along with other criteria to get your wallet whitelisted). 

Again, just my very basic and possibly not completely accurate understanding of how these things work. As usual, always DYOR

Yes with Launchpads you essentially are paying a third party for a proxy claim of legitimacy and for marketing of the token you're investing in, although they don't even do that much to be honest

You could also argue that these things can also be done more organically, and/or more decentralized manner which would of course bring down the costs involved. Such a model will be the future in cardano's ecosystems as Catalyst evolves I strongly believe, as well as keeping the more established launchpads.

For example marketing of projects can be done easily be done by the community, already is being, through social media sharing on twitter and blogs etc. Such things can even be incentivized with tokens, although people like us do it regardless.

Vetting of projects is more tricky, and would still require human knowhow of people in tech and people who can do thorough reasearch and investigation of projects and people. But these things can easily be incorperated in a decentralized way incentivising the right people to complete the tasks and getting all of them reach consensus, people may even finding themselves with jobs doing this kind of thing.
